*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30: 2 of 11 stories closed, 1 PASSING (US-561), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560). NEXT ITERATION PICKS UP US-563 (drive_summary, size L) -- nothing blocks it. ***

*** US-561 CLOSED passes:true -- watchdog honesty. All FOUR of Atlas's 08-17 section-3 defects dispositioned (AC-3 explicitly forbids fixing one and closing): 3a FIXED, 3b FIXED, 3c DEFERRED WITH CAUSE + the false claim it had produced corrected in place, 3d observability FIXED / policy deliberately unchanged. Full per-defect detail is in sprint.json completionNotes; the reusable lessons are below. ***

THE LOAD-BEARING FIX (3a): the threshold IS the defect, and the fix is never a bigger number. `DEFAULT_ERROR_THRESHOLD=100` was calibrated against a ~30,000-marker/window catastrophic wedge, but the regime the CIO drove into runs 84-101 -- so the constant sat INSIDE the signal's own operating band and two consecutive ticks of ONE continuous freeze logged `WEDGED -- 101 markers` then `healthy; markers=84`. Replaced with PRESENCE + DWELL: healthy was MEASURED as exactly zero, which makes zero the BOUNDARY of the band rather than a point inside it -- so any marker at all means the class is live, and 60s (two timer ticks) of UNBROKEN presence means wedged. **There is no magnitude left to mis-calibrate.** `100` survives only as `DEFAULT_MARKER_READ_CAP`, an I/O bound, and a STRUCTURAL test forbids it re-entering `decideAction`.

*** GENERALISE THIS -- IT IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL AT THRESHOLD+DWELL ON THIS PROJECT (Spool's coolant fan-cycle ceiling, the US-564 bit-identity gate, now the watchdog). THE TELL IS ALWAYS THE SAME: TWO SAMPLES OF THE SAME STATE DISAGREE. When you see it, do not retune -- go find what was MEASURED for the healthy case. If that value sits at the EDGE of the band (zero markers, zero distinct values, exactly-0.0 LTFT), presence/identity replaces magnitude and the tuned constant disappears entirely. If it sits INSIDE the band, you need dwell. ***

3b, AND THE US-560 LESSON PAYING OFF IMMEDIATELY: `journalctl --grep` EXITS 1 WHEN NOTHING MATCHED -- which on a healthy kiosk is every single tick -- so US-523 reported a clean kiosk as `journal_unreadable`. That is the exact INVERSE of its own docstring ('0 == readable and clean, None if it could not be read'): the instrument could not report its own good news, and a genuinely broken journal was indistinguishable from a working one. Fix MEASURES readability (`journalIsReadable()`, one unfiltered `journalctl --lines=1`, failure-path only) instead of inferring it from an overloaded exit code. **I re-measured BOTH halves live on the Pi rather than inheriting Atlas's read: grep -> RC=1 with EMPTY stdout; unfiltered probe -> RC=0.** One ssh, ~20 seconds. Honest bound recorded: I ran as mcornelison over ssh, NOT inside the unit's cgroup/SupplementaryGroups, so I measured the exit-code behaviour and not the unit's exact journal scope.

3c IS THE ONE I DID NOT FIX, AND THE INTERESTING PART IS WHAT I DID INSTEAD. The ~3min lag is structural: markers appear when an allocation is finally ATTEMPTED, not when painting stops (froze ~16:15, burst 16:18:32). Nothing inside a journal-reading watchdog can close that -- it needs a signal that LEADS rather than lags, i.e. a repaint heartbeat published BY the page, which is a dashboard story. **But the stale claim it had produced was live in the repo**: eclipse-kiosk-watchdog.timer's header asserted 'a wedge is seen within about one window and recovered inside ~1.5 min'. Corrected in place, and the honest bound is now stated in the module header. GENERALISE: when you defer a defect, go find the CLAIMS it falsified and correct those -- a deferred defect that leaves a confident wrong sentence in a header is worse than the defect.

3d: the budget POLICY is unchanged (Atlas called it correct); what AC-5 actually names is that 2 of 5 restarts were consumed mid-drive and nothing surfaced it. Now stated on EVERY tick as 'N of M restarts this hour (K left)', at WARNING once any is consumed and INFO while untouched -- both directions pinned, because if every 30s tick warned, the WARNING would carry no information. NOT DONE and flagged rather than silently skipped: surfacing it ON THE PANEL needs a state file under /run/eclipse-obd/states/, and **this unit must NEVER declare RuntimeDirectory=eclipse-obd -- systemd would DELETE that directory, including the live states/ the emitters write, when the oneshot exits.** Real constraint, documented in the unit header; panel surfacing is a separate story.

NEW FAIL-SAFE WORTH REMEMBERING: adding state to a detector adds a failure mode to the DETECTOR. The dwell lives in the ledger, so an unwritable ledger means the watchdog has lost its memory -- and the pre-existing 'no restart, carry on' path would have logged `healthy` from a detector that could no longer detect. Markers-present + unwritable-ledger now returns LEDGER_UNWRITABLE (exit 2), never healthy. **Any new persisted state needs its own not-healthy path.** Also: a corrupt clock is worse than no clock -- JSON `true` floats to 1.0 and reads as a 56-year dwell, restarting the panel on the next single marker (the US-517 trap, now pinned over 4 junk shapes).

PROCESS GOTCHAS FROM THIS ITERATION: (1) An ImportError/collection error masks every per-test reason -- landing the NAME skeleton first (constants, dataclass fields, inert stubs, OLD behaviour) turned one useless red into **24 behavioural reds**. Same trick as US-554; worth the extra run every time. (2) **Two of my new tests went GREEN against the skeleton for the WRONG reason** (the old threshold happened to route them identically) -- scan the red list for tests that SHOULD be failing and are not, BEFORE implementing. (3) My gate caught an error in my own TEST, not the code: `runOnce` reports the OUTCOME (`wedge_restarted`) while `decideAction` reports the DECISION (`wedge_detected`); asserting the decision vocabulary on a runOnce result would have gone green ONLY IF THE RESTART FAILED. Check which layer's vocabulary you are asserting in. (4) Three pins MOVED, not deleted, each repointed docstring saying what it used to assert -- deleting them erases the record of what changed.

VALIDATION STILL OWED ON US-561 (hardware, not closable here): validationCriteria #1 wants the display deliberately wedged and the verdict watched across several ticks. That needs the code DEPLOYED to the Pi. The 5-tick replay test reproduces Atlas's observed counts in software -- evidence about the discriminator, NOT about the live box. I did not claim it.

ENVIRONMENT (carried forward, all re-confirmed this session): **THE PI IS REACHABLE** -- `ssh -o BatchMode=yes chi-eclipse-01` works, no password; deploy tree is `/home/mcornelison/Projects/Eclipse-01`. RE-TEST AN ENVIRONMENTAL CLAIM BEFORE INHERITING IT. `make` is NOT on PATH (exits 127, **which reads like a pass**) -- use `python -m ruff check <file>`. `mypy` is NOT installed. **COMPOUND BASH IS REFUSED** (`a; b` and `a && b` both) -- one command per call; **and `cd X && cmd > file` is refused specifically**, so redirect from the default cwd. `/tmp` is NOT writable -- scratch files go inside the repo and must be rm'd before committing. `pytest -q` prints NO summary line on this tree: redirect, then `echo $?` AND `grep -cE '^(FAILED|ERROR)'`; get a count via `--collect-only -q | tail -1`. On the Pi, `xxd`/`edid-decode` are NOT installed but `python3` is. The index lock was CLEAR all session.

--- US-560 (Session 1, this sprint) SUMMARY: passes:false, premise REFUTED BY HARDWARE, BL-034 filed, needs an ATLAS RULING. The OSOYOO HDMI35 does not advertise 480x320 in its EDID -- it is a SCALER panel (480x320 glass behind a chip that takes standard HDMI timings), so there IS no native mode and 720p IS the shipping configuration. Root cause of the false premise was a FABRICATED TEST FIXTURE in US-552 asserting a hardware fact nobody had read, which made its own suite unfalsifiable. **STILL FLAGGED TO PM, UNANSWERED, AND IT AFFECTS US-555/556/557 THIS SPRINT: the chromium kiosk runs with NO --window-size and NO --force-device-scale-factor, so the dashboard renders into a ~1280x720 CSS-px viewport while US-557's band budget is ~320-canvas arithmetic. Someone must measure the actual viewport before the chrome stories run.** Full detail in sprint.json US-560 completionNotes + progress.txt. ---
